rules.title: Diagnostic: The rules of the Layered Architecture should be followed
rules.rationale: Traditional layering (application accessed only by incoming adapters) contradicts Ports and Adapters, where outgoing adapters implement application-level output ports; the hexagonal rules cover the intended dependency direction
rules.selects: Informational - selects nothing.
rules.checks: Informational - carries doctrine only. The dependency direction is held by the crate graph and the hexagonal rules.

rules.title: Domain must not have dependencies on Infrastructure
rules.rationale: Domain should not depend on infrastructure concerns (Dependency Inversion Principle)
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain, the shared kernel's domain crate included.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = infrastructure or bootstrap. The compiler then refuses every use of such a crate; the graph test refuses the Cargo.toml line.

rules.title: Application Services must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rules.rationale: Application services should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = application.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = infrastructure or bootstrap, its own context's included.

rules.title: Transaction boundaries belong to the application layer
rules.rationale: Transactions are an application-layer concern - domain and incoming adapters must not manage them
rules.selects: Paths in every module of every crate with a layer that name the building-block trait TransactionBoundary (wiring) or one of the types [workspace.metadata.dca] transaction-types lists (transaction use), written crate::Type - the crate and the type's name are compared, the modules between are not. The default preset: sqlx::Transaction, diesel::connection::AnsiTransactionManager, sea_orm::DatabaseTransaction, rusqlite::Transaction, tokio_postgres::Transaction, mongodb::ClientSession. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Transaction use sits in an application crate or in the outgoing module of an adapters crate; wiring sits there or in an infrastructure or bootstrap crate. A domain, api or events crate (the shared kernel's domain crate included), an incoming adapter or another module of an adapters crate that names one is reported, once per path. Rust has no declarative transaction attribute, so there is no annotation selection; a call that runs a transaction without naming the type (a method on a pool) is not seen. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: No implementation is placed into the building-blocks output-port package
rules.rationale: port.out contains outbound port interfaces (Repository, OutputPort, DomainEventPublisher) shared across all bounded contexts. These must be interfaces to ensure the application layer remains framework-independent and follows the Dependency Inversion Principle. Implementations belong in infrastructure or adapter packages.
rules.selects: Items in the building blocks' port module.
rules.checks: A crate cannot add an item to another crate's module, so the building blocks' output-port module holds what the library declares and nothing a project adds. The rule holds by the language.

rules.title: Diagnostic: classes of a module that sit in no layer
rules.rationale: Every rule written for a layer selects by the layer a class is placed in. A class of a module that sits in none - a mapper or a persistence entity beside the adapter packages, a class whose layer is declared only on its neighbour - is seen by none of them
rules.selects: In a crate that carries a context but no layer (the two-crate form), every top-level module.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every top-level module that is none of domain, application, adapters, api, events and infrastructure, and never fails. In the crate-per-layer form every item sits in a layer by its crate and nothing is listed.

rules.title: Application layer must not use persistence or transaction APIs
rules.rationale: A use case declares its transaction with the configured transactional annotation or draws its boundary through the transaction-boundary port or a decorator around the use case, never through a persistence context, a connection or a transaction scope of its own. A persistence or transaction API in the application layer binds the use cases to one persistence technology and hides where the boundary is; the boundary's implementation is the single place that knows how to open and commit a transaction
rules.selects: Every application crate and its normal Cargo dependencies.
rules.checks: None is a crate [workspace.metadata.dca] persistence-crates lists (package names; sqlx, diesel, sea-orm, rusqlite, tokio-postgres and mongodb by default). Without the dependency the compiler refuses every use of the crate.

rules.title: Domain must not access Application Services (Onion Architecture - Domain is innermost layer)
rules.rationale: Domain is the innermost layer in onion architecture and should not depend on application services
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = application, its own context's included.

rules.title: The Domain Model should be framework independent and should not use 3rd party libraries when possible
rules.rationale: Domain should be framework-independent (Dependency Inversion Principle)
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain, the shared kernel's domain crate included.
rules.checks: Its normal dependencies are the building blocks, the domain crates of its own context and of the shared kernel, and the configured allowed crates only (by default none). Dev-dependencies are not counted. cargo-deny can refuse known framework crates workspace-wide; the graph test is the per-crate check.

rules.title: Domain models must not carry prohibited framework derives or attributes
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Types in a domain crate, the shared kernel's included: structs, enums, their fields and enum variants, the impl blocks for them - inherent and of traits - and the methods in those blocks.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type, its fields, its variants, its impl blocks or their methods. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Domain layer must stay synchronous
rules.rationale: Asynchrony is an I/O concern of ports and adapters; a synchronous domain model stays testable, deterministic and free of sync-over-async hazards
rules.selects: Every module of every domain crate. Exempt from the async part: the traits that carry the DomainGateway or the DomainService role, with their methods, and the impl blocks of types that implement DomainService. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Outside the exempt items no function is async, returns or takes a type named Future, BoxFuture or ScopedBoxFuture (a parameter's type, impl Future included, or a bound of the function's generics), no field holds one (Pin<Box<dyn Future>>), and no expression awaits or builds an async block; nowhere in the domain crate does a path name a crate [workspace.metadata.dca] async-runtime-crates lists (tokio, async-std, futures and smol by default). This diverges from Java and .NET, whose domain is synchronous throughout: in Rust a domain gateway answers asynchronously, so the gateways and the domain services that await them are async, std's Future and nothing more; aggregates, entities, values, events, failures, factories and specifications stay synchronous. DCA-RS-004 holds the signatures alone. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Classes from the domain should not access port adapters
rules.rationale: Domain should not depend on adapters (ports and adapters pattern)
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = adapters, of any context.

rules.title: Application Services should not access port adapters
rules.rationale: Application services should only depend on domain and outbound ports, not adapters
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = application.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = adapters, of any context.

rules.title: Controllers and Resources must never access repositories directly
rules.rationale: Controllers must go through use cases (input ports), never directly to repositories
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No item names a trait that carries the repository role or a type that implements one. Other output ports are not checked. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Incoming Adapters must only use outbound ports (not infrastructure implementations)
rules.rationale: Incoming adapters should only use outbound ports declared as interfaces (port.out), not infrastructure implementation details
rules.selects: The incoming module of every adapters crate. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No item names a path into a crate with layer = infrastructure or bootstrap. The graph test refuses the dependency where the whole adapters crate must not have it; the source test refuses the use in the incoming module where the outgoing module may. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Outgoing adapters must not use another module's infrastructure
rules.rationale: Technical infrastructure reuse preserves module isolation
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = adapters.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate with layer = infrastructure of another context.

rules.title: Incoming port adapters must not depend directly on outgoing port adapters within the same context
rules.rationale: Port adapters should communicate through application services, not directly (event consumers are the exception)
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate, the configured event-consumer submodule excluded. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No item names a path into the outgoing module of the same crate. The compiler cannot hold this: both modules are one crate. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Incoming adapters depend on no other module, except event consumers on the events they subscribe to
rules.rationale: An incoming adapter drives its own module only: a controller that needs a sibling's data goes through its own use case, output port and outgoing adapter to the sibling's published api - only a subscription legitimately meets a foreign contract on the incoming side
rules.selects: The incoming module of every crate with layer = adapters (one crate per layer), and every module below it.
rules.checks: No module there names a path into a crate of another context, the configured event-consumer submodule (event-consumer-module) excepted. The crate's own dependencies on another context are DCA-STR-006's graph check. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Classes named *Repository must reside in the outgoing adapter package (name-based discovery of unmarked repositories)
rules.rationale: Repository implementations are secondary adapters (outgoing ports)
rules.selects: Structs and enums in every crate whose name ends with Repository. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Each sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Output Ports in application.shared must extend OutputPort
rules.rationale: Top-level interfaces in application.shared are output ports and must extend OutputPort to be part of the port hierarchy. Nested interfaces (e.g. IdentityProvider.Identity) are part of their enclosing port's contract, not ports themselves
rules.selects: Traits in the shared module of every application crate. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Each carries the output-port role, through OutputPort or one of its sub-traits (Repository, Store, the event publishers).

rules.title: Output ports must not reside in the domain layer
rules.rationale: output ports (Repository, Store, OutputPort) are an application-layer concern and must live in application/shared/, not domain/
rules.selects: Traits in every crate that carry the output-port role. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: None sits in a domain crate. A domain crate sees the building blocks and could declare one; the compiler does not refuse it.

rules.title: Incoming Adapters must depend on input port interfaces, not on use case classes
rules.rationale: A driving adapter drives the application through its port. Injecting the concrete implementation instead couples the adapter to one realisation of the use case, defeats the Dependency Inversion Principle the port exists for, and makes the adapter untestable without the real use case and everything it depends on
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate, event consumers included. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No item names a type that implements an input port; naming the input-port trait is what the rule expects. The use case type stays pub because bootstrap constructs it, so visibility cannot hold this. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Incoming Adapters must not depend on domain services
rules.rationale: An incoming adapter translates external input, calls an input port and formats its result. Injecting or invoking a domain service bypasses the application boundary; the use case owns that collaboration and puts its outcome into the result. Outgoing adapters are outside this rule - repositories and other driven adapters may construct or reconstitute domain objects while implementing output ports
rules.selects: Items in the incoming module of every adapters crate. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No item names a type that carries the domain-service role. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Outgoing Adapters must not depend on input ports
rules.rationale: An outgoing adapter is driven: the application calls it through an output port. One that calls an input port drives the application instead - it is an incoming adapter filed on the wrong side, and the call it makes runs a second use case from inside the first one's outgoing edge
rules.selects: Items in the outgoing module of every adapters crate. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No item names a trait that carries the input-port role or a type that implements one. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: GET handlers must not drive an input port that takes a command
rules.rationale: A state-changing use case is reached only by an unsafe HTTP method, never by GET. Links, prefetching, crawlers and cross-site navigation issue GET requests on their own; a GET that runs a command changes state nobody asked to change. A handler that names no HTTP method answers GET as well
rules.selects: Handler functions in the incoming module of every adapters crate that a router preset named in [workspace.metadata.dca] routers registers for GET: axum - a free function passed to a routing function of axum (get(show)) or to get chained on one (post(create).get(show)); actix-web - one passed to .to(..) on web::get(), or one carrying #[get(..)] or #[route(..)] with GET; rocket - one carrying #[get(..)] or #[route(..)] with GET. Without a preset nothing is selected. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No such function names, in its signature or body, a type of an application crate whose name ends with Command - the input of a command port - and none calls a method on an input port that takes a command (a trait with the input-port role whose UseCase<..> input or a method parameter is a ...Command type, or a type that implements one): a parameter, a local binding whose type is written out, a field of a parameter's struct, or a local bound to one of these by a straight-line let. The same holds for the free functions of the handler's module it calls, one level deep. Not seen: a helper of another module or a method, a call through more than one helper, and a receiver whose type the suite cannot resolve; a handler registered through a router another crate builds is found when that crate is in the workspace. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Diagnostic: adapters that publish an enum by its member name
rules.rationale: A value an adapter publishes from an enum is spelled explicitly - a code per value on the enum or a mapping in the adapter - never derived from the member's name. Renaming a member is a refactoring inside the code and must not change what a client reads
rules.selects: Function bodies in every adapters crate, and in them the enums declared in a domain or application crate: a parameter, a written-out local or a field of self of such a type, and a path to one of its variants. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every .to_string() on such an enum and every argument formatted with ? ({:?}, {:#?}, {0:?}, {name:?}, captured or named) by format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln!, panic! or format_args!, and never fails. A serializer that writes the variant name, and an enum reached through an unannotated local, are not seen.

rules.title: Event listeners that drive an input port must run after the commit in their own transaction
rules.rationale: A reaction to an event changes state or performs an external effect through a use case. Run inside the transaction that raised the event, it changes a second aggregate in the first one's transaction, a failure in the reaction rolls back the fact that caused it, and a retry of the request runs the reaction again. A listener that only translates or measures calls output ports and may run in that transaction
rules.selects: Types that implement the building-block trait EventListener<E, U> - a listener that reacts inside the publishing transaction, reaching its output ports through the unit U - and not TransactionalEventListener<E>. What reaches an input port: a field whose type, through generic arguments and the bounds of the struct and of its impl blocks, names a trait that carries the input-port role or a type that implements one; in the body of its on method, a parameter, a written-out local, a field of self of such a type, a field of a parameter whose type is a struct of the workspace holding one, and any path that names one.
rules.checks: No such listener reaches an input port: a listener that drives a use case implements TransactionalEventListener<E>, so it is delivered after the commit, in a transaction of its own. Rust has no listener annotation; the two building-block traits are the declaration. A call through a helper of the listener's own is not followed.

rules.title: Controllers must reside in an incoming adapter package
rules.rationale: A controller turns a request into a command or a query and is an incoming adapter. Outside the incoming adapter packages it is outside the selection of every rule written for incoming adapters - the GET-handler rule, the controller naming rules, the boundary rules - and passes them all
rules.selects: Handler functions the router presets named in [workspace.metadata.dca] routers register, anywhere in the workspace, read as DCA-HEX-014 reads them, for every verb. Without a preset nothing is selected. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Each is declared in the incoming module of an adapters crate. Rust handlers are functions, not classes; a method registered as a handler is not seen.

rules.title: Output port implementations are placed in the outgoing adapters
rules.rationale: An output port is what the application needs from outside; whatever implements it is an outgoing adapter - the implemented port says so. An implementation placed in the infrastructure package, the application, the domain or in no layer at all is outside the selection of every rule written for outgoing adapters, and infrastructure then holds behaviour instead of wiring alone
rules.selects: Every impl of a trait that carries the output-port role. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: The implementing type sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate, or it is the bridge in an infrastructure or bootstrap crate: a type that names an input port - a field whose type, through generic arguments and the bounds of the type and its impl blocks, names a trait that carries the input-port role or a type that implements one, or such a bound itself - and so answers the output port by driving a use case. The orphan rule already keeps the impl out of the domain crate, which cannot see the application's port; a test double in the application crate is reported.

rules.title: Diagnostic: incoming adapters that read the caller's roles in their own code
rules.rationale: A check that reads nothing but the caller's roles or claims - is this caller staff? - is a property of the exposure and is declared on the route, with the framework's authorization annotation, where a reader of the route sees it and the framework answers an unauthenticated and an unauthorized caller apart. A branch on the caller's roles inside the adapter's code hides the gate and renders whatever status the branch writes. A check that needs the stored data - is this yours? - is not claims-only and belongs to the use case
rules.selects: Functions and methods in the incoming module of every adapters crate, and the router expressions of those crates. Nothing is selected when [workspace.metadata.dca] names neither authorization-extractors (types whose presence in a handler's signature declares a claims-only check, such as a RequireRole<R> extractor) nor authorization-layers (functions whose call in a router's .layer(...) or .route_layer(...) declares it for the routes added before it); both are empty by default. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every call in a body, as a method or as a path, named has_role, has_any_role, has_authority, has_any_authority, is_in_role or is_user_in_role, and never fails. A function whose signature names a configured extractor, or whose name appears in the receiver of a .layer(...)/.route_layer(...) call that calls a configured layer function within the same crate, is not listed. Not seen: a handler routed behind a layer in a router another crate builds, a role compared by the handler itself (roles.contains(...)), and a helper of the project's own declared outside the incoming module. Rust has no route annotation; the extractor and the layer are its declarative forms.

rules.title: Outgoing adapters must not call state-changing methods of aggregate roots
rules.rationale: An aggregate's state changes through its own methods, each with its guard and its event, and the application decides when one runs. An outgoing adapter that calls one changes the aggregate on a path no use case owns, outside the transaction the use case draws and without the events it publishes. The adapter stores and loads what the aggregate holds
rules.selects: Function bodies in the outgoing module of every adapters crate. Nothing is selected when no type implements AggregateRoot. Layers are read from crates with a layer (one crate per layer); in the two-crate form - a context crate without a layer whose layers are top-level modules - this rule reads no layer.
rules.checks: No body calls, on a parameter, a local binding whose type is written out or a field of self whose type names a type that implements AggregateRoot - or on a local bound without a written type to Type::function(..) of that type returning Self or the type (after ? or .await, a Result or Option of it), or to one of these by a straight-line let, until a later let shadows the name - a method of that type that takes &mut self - in Rust the receiver says which methods change the aggregate. A method of a building-block trait (clearing the recorded events after publishing) passes. A change written to storage directly, past the aggregate, and a call on an unannotated local initialised otherwise (a method's return value) are not seen.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must implement AggregateRoot<T, ID>
rules.rationale: Classes named *AggregateRoot must implement AggregateRoot interface (DDD pattern)
rules.selects: Structs and enums in every domain crate, the shared kernel's included, whose name ends with AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: The type implements AggregateRoot. Rust names rarely carry the suffix; selection by name stays as in Java.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must not hold references to Repositories or other Output Ports
rules.rationale: Aggregates are persistence-ignorant: use cases retrieve facts; external calculations belong in domain services over supplied snapshots. Review callback parameters manually; this field check cannot prove semantic responsibility
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field type, generic arguments and Box<dyn ...> included, names a trait with the output-port role. The project's own ports live in the application crate, which the domain crate cannot see; the source test holds the building blocks' own port traits.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must not have fields with other Aggregate Root types
rules.rationale: Vernon's Aggregate Design Rule #3: reference other Aggregates by identity to keep aggregate boundaries and transactional consistency intact
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field type, through Vec, Option, Box and other generic arguments, is a type that implements AggregateRoot. References by id pass.

rules.title: Entities must have an ID field
rules.rationale: An Entity is defined by its identity, which is a value object implementing the Id marker
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity, aggregate roots included.
rules.checks: The trait's associated type Id is bound to the Id marker, so the compiler holds the typed identity. The source test checks that a field of exactly that type exists - the type the impl Entity binds to Id, compared resolved, references stripped; a collection of ids (Vec<PartId>) is no id - so the id is state, not computed. An enum entity holds it in every variant, directly or in the workspace struct the variant wraps. When the binding cannot be read, any field whose type names a type that implements Id counts.

rules.title: Entities must not be instantiated directly from outside the aggregate
rules.rationale: Entities are created through their aggregate root so that the root can enforce its invariants
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity but not AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: The type has no pub field and no pub associated function that returns Self; pub(crate) and private ones pass. Nor can it be built wherever it is visible without a function of its own: no impl of Default, From<..> or TryFrom<..> (a trait of the workspace with that name excepted), no #[derive(Default)], and a pub enum has no open variant - a unit variant and one with named fields are constructors wherever the enum is visible, a tuple variant is one unless every field it wraps is a workspace struct whose fields are all private (a state only its own module builds), so a state machine of sealed states passes. With private fields no code outside the aggregate's module can build one by struct literal - the compiler holds that part. Java checks who calls the constructor; Rust checks the visibility of every way in, so a pub(crate) way used outside the aggregate passes.

rules.title: Domain model classes must not have public setter methods
rules.rationale: Behavior-rich domain models change state through intention-revealing methods from the ubiquitous language, never through public setters
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity, aggregate roots included, with their methods. A type's methods are, as Java reads a class's: its inherent methods and the methods of its impls of workspace traits, a workspace trait's default methods the impl does not write out included; impls of std, core, external and building-block traits are not read.
rules.checks: No pub method named set_<name> takes &mut self and exactly one further parameter and returns ().

rules.title: Entities must not have fields with Aggregate Root types
rules.rationale: An entity inside an aggregate references other aggregates by identity only, otherwise the aggregate boundary leaks
rules.selects: Types that implement Entity but not AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field type, through generic arguments, is a type that implements AggregateRoot.

rules.title: Value Objects must not contain Aggregate Roots or Entities
rules.rationale: A Value Object is defined by its attributes; holding an object with identity would give it a lifecycle it must not have
rules.selects: Types that implement Value. Names resolve as the compiler resolves them: a use inside a function body counts for the module only where the module neither declares nor imports the name, and a glob over an enum (use Seal::*;) brings in its variants only.
rules.checks: No field type, through generic arguments, is a type that implements Entity or AggregateRoot.

rules.reason: Rust has no inheritance; a struct cannot be extended, so a value object is final by construction.

rules.title: Value Objects must not mutate their state
rules.rationale: Records have implicitly final fields and enums are immutable by design; a hand-written value class must make every instance field final itself
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self, no field is pub, and no field type is an interior-mutability type (Cell, RefCell, Mutex, RwLock, atomics). Rust has no final field; immutability is the absence of a mutating API.

rules.title: Value Objects must not have setter methods
rules.rationale: Value Objects are immutable; state changes produce a new instance instead of mutating
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: No method is named set_<name>, whatever its receiver.

rules.title: Value Objects must be records or immutable classes with attribute equality
rules.rationale: A record grants attribute-based equality for free; a hand-written Value Object class must override equals and hashCode itself to compare by its attributes
rules.selects: Types that implement Value.
rules.checks: The building-block trait Value has PartialEq as supertrait, so the compiler refuses a value object without equality. Whether the equality compares every attribute is not decidable; a derive is the expected form. Immutability is DCA-TAC-010's.

rules.title: Repository Interfaces should extend Repository Marker Interface
rules.rationale: Repository interfaces should extend Repository marker interface
rules.selects: Traits in every application crate whose name ends with Repository.
rules.checks: The trait carries the repository role.

rules.title: Repository interfaces must reside in the application layer (local to a use case or shared)
rules.rationale: Repository interfaces are output ports in the application layer (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits that carry the repository role, the building block excluded.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate, the shared kernel's application crate included.

rules.title: Repository Implementations must reside in adapter.outgoing package
rules.rationale: Repository implementations are outgoing adapters in bounded contexts
rules.selects: Types that implement a trait with the repository role.
rules.checks: Each sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Repositories must only exist for Aggregate Roots
rules.rationale: A repository is the collection of one aggregate type; a repository for an entity would let callers bypass the root that guards the aggregate's invariants
rules.selects: Traits with the repository role (through Repository<T>) whose name ends with Repository.
rules.checks: The bound Repository<T: AggregateRoot> makes a repository for anything but a root unkompilable. The source test checks the name: the trait is named after the type it binds plus Repository.

rules.title: Repository methods must not return non-root Entities
rules.rationale: A caller receiving an Entity that is not an Aggregate Root could mutate part of an aggregate without passing its root, so the root's invariants would never run
rules.selects: Traits with the repository role.
rules.checks: No method of the trait returns a type, through generic arguments, that implements Entity but not AggregateRoot. A pub(crate) entity cannot be named by the application crate at all.

rules.title: Store interfaces must extend the Store marker, not Repository
rules.rationale: Stores extend the Store marker; Repository is reserved for Aggregate Roots
rules.selects: Traits outside adapters and infrastructure crates whose name ends with Store.
rules.checks: The trait carries the store role and not the repository role.

rules.title: Store interfaces must reside in the application layer (local to a use case or shared)
rules.rationale: Store interfaces are output ports in the application layer (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits that carry the store role, the building block excluded.
rules.checks: Each sits in an application crate, the shared kernel's application crate included.

rules.title: Store implementations must reside in the adapter.outgoing package
rules.rationale: Store implementations are outgoing adapters in bounded contexts
rules.selects: Types that implement a trait with the store role.
rules.checks: Each sits in the outgoing module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Store interfaces must not declare save or delete methods
rules.rationale: save/delete are Repository semantics; a Store that has them is a Repository wearing the wrong name, and the stored object should then be an Aggregate Root
rules.selects: Traits that carry the store role.
rules.checks: No method declared on the trait itself is named save, delete or delete_by_id.

rules.title: Aggregate Roots must not expose a public struct literal
rules.rationale: An aggregate comes into being in two ways - created as a business fact or reconstituted from storage - and each is a named factory method. A public constructor is a third, unnamed way that skips the creation invariants and the event creation raises
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot.
rules.checks: No field is pub, and no unnamed way builds it: no impl of Default, From<..> or TryFrom<..> (a trait of the workspace with that name excepted), no #[derive(Default)], and a pub enum has no open variant - a unit variant and one with named fields are constructors wherever the enum is visible, a tuple variant is one unless every field it wraps is a workspace struct whose fields are all private (a state only its own module builds), so a state machine of sealed states passes. Rust has no constructor; the struct literal is the constructor, and private fields keep it inside the aggregate's module. The root's associated functions (create, place, ...) are its named factories and check invariants.

rules.title: Value Objects must not declare a neutral factory beside an origin factory with the same parameters
rules.rationale: A value built from input and a value rebuilt from storage are two origins with different checks - validated and derived on the way in, taken as given on the way back - and each has its own named factory. A second factory that takes the same parameters, such as a neutral of(...) beside them, leaves the caller to guess which checks run
rules.selects: Types that implement Value and their pub associated functions returning Self.
rules.checks: No function named new takes the same parameter types, in the same order, as another such function. Types are compared resolved, references and lifetimes stripped: &'a str and &str, String and std::string::String are the same; a type of the workspace compares by the type a path resolves to. Two named origins (from_input, from_stored) pass.

rules.title: Domain types must not hold bare primitives, strings or time types; a boolean only as a field or a predicate
rules.rationale: A value with rules of its own - a postal code, a quantity, a moment, an identifier - is a value object; held as a bare String, int, Instant or UUID its validation is repeated at every use or missing. A value object with several components holds value objects too; only a wrapper - a value of exactly one component - holds the primitive it wraps. A single yes/no fact may stay a boolean field: the type is told (complete()) and answers (isCompleted()). A boolean parameter is a flag argument - setCompleted(true) lets the caller set the state instead of triggering the behaviour - except in the factory that rebuilds a stored object, which hands the stored fact back to the type that holds it. Three or more states, or transitions with rules, are an enum or a value
rules.selects: Structs, enums and traits in every domain crate, the shared kernel's included: the fields of structs and enum variants, the signatures of inherent methods - private ones included - and of the methods a trait declares; an impl of a trait is read where the trait is declared. Not selected: a single-field newtype that implements Value or Id, failures, and trait methods of a building block.
rules.checks: No field, parameter or return type, through generic arguments, is String, &str, a primitive, a time type (std::time::SystemTime, chrono, time) or a bare Uuid. A private field of type bool - a single yes/no fact - and a bool return - a predicate - pass; a bool parameter and a pub bool struct field, flag arguments, do not. A bool parameter of the factory that rebuilds a stored value - an associated function without a receiver that returns Self or the type, named as [workspace.metadata.dca] reconstituting-factories lists, reconstitute and restore by default, case ignored - passes; its other parameters are checked. A returned impl Future is read by its Output. A domain enum with exactly two fieldless variants that name one fact and its negation is a boolean in disguise and is reported where it is declared: the pairs Yes/No, True/False, On/Off, Present/Absent, Enabled/Disabled, and any X with NotX, NoX or NonX, and UnX where X is adjective-like - it ends in -ed, -able, -ible, -ive, -ent, -ant, -al or -ful (Locked/Unlocked) - (case and underscores ignored). Java takes UnX for any X; Rust reads UnX before a verb as its reverse action, so Lock/Unlock, Load/Unload, Follow/Unfollow and Do/Undo pass. Two variants with names of their own (Open/Closed) pass.

rules.title: The repository of an owned aggregate declares a lookup by the aggregate's id and the owner's id
rules.rationale: An object loaded by its id alone is reachable by anyone who knows or guesses the id - the insecure direct object reference of broken access control (OWASP Top 10, A01). An aggregate marked as owned belongs to someone; its repository offers a lookup scoped to the owner, so a use case acting for a caller can load it through the caller and an unscoped lookup is never the only way in. Whether the use case calls the scoped lookup, and whether it proved the caller's right to a change of owner, is logic the rule does not see
rules.selects: Types that implement both Owned and AggregateRoot, each with the repository traits that bind it through Repository<T>. The owner id type is the type the impl Owned block binds to OwnerId (the trait requires it, and requires AggregateRoot as supertrait); the aggregate's id is the type its impl Entity binds to Id. An owned aggregate without a repository trait is not selected.
rules.checks: At least one method the repository trait declares itself takes a parameter whose type (through references) is the aggregate's id type and a further parameter whose type is the owner id type - either position, any name - and returns a type that names the aggregate, through Result, Option or another wrapper. A method that answers only yes or no does not count; the inherited find_by_id takes the id alone. An owner id type the suite cannot resolve (a type outside the workspace, a type alias) is reported. Whether a use case calls the scoped lookup is not checked; a lookup declared only in a generic intermediate trait is not seen. An empty selection passes.

rules.title: Aggregates, entities, values, factories and specifications receive a domain gateway only as a parameter
rules.rationale: A domain gateway only reads: it supplies a fact the model does not hold or a computation bound to a technology. A model method that needs it takes it as a parameter, so the dependency stands in the signature and the caller - a domain service or the use case - decides which implementation answers. A gateway held in a field makes the model stateful towards the outside and survives into every later call; a gateway looked up from a registry or built in place is a hidden dependency no signature shows. The service-locator form - a static registry the model asks for its services - is the one this rule rejects
rules.selects: Types that implement AggregateRoot, Entity, Value or Factory, and specifications (types that implement Specification or whose name ends with Specification); a type that itself implements DomainGateway is not selected. Read: their fields, through generic arguments and the type's bounds, the return types of their methods, and the paths their method bodies use as values - expression paths, called functions, struct literals - a name the body binds (a parameter, a let, a closure or match binding) shadowing an item of the same name.
rules.checks: A type that names a trait carrying the DomainGateway role, or a type that implements one, appears in none of these places: a field; the return type of a method; a function or an associated function the body calls whose declared return type names a gateway - a registry or locator - an associated function of a trait included, called through the trait's path, <T as Trait>::f or a generic parameter bounded by the trait; a field the body reads from another value (ctx.rates, self.context.rates) whose type is known - a parameter or a local with its type written out, or a field of self - when that value's struct holds a gateway in the field; a static or a const the body reads whose type names a gateway; an implementation the body constructs (a struct literal, a unit or tuple struct, an associated function of the implementation). A gateway taken as a method parameter and the calls made on it pass. A domain service and the application may use the gateway freely. The model is synchronous (DCA-ONI-004): it can call only a gateway whose methods are synchronous - a hasher, a converter; an asynchronous gateway is awaited by a domain service, which hands the model the answer. Not seen: a method called on a value that returns a gateway, a field read from a value whose type is not written out (an unannotated local, a return value, a closure parameter) or from a generic parameter, a trait function whose return type names the gateway only through an associated type, and a gateway hidden behind a type alias.

rules.title: Diagnostic: Display discovered bounded contexts
rules.rationale: Making the discovered contexts visible shows which packages the strategic rules govern
rules.selects: Every crate whose [package.metadata.dca] carries a context or shared-kernel = true.
rules.checks: Informational - lists each context with its crates and their layers, and the shared kernel's crates with their layers, and never fails.

rules.title: Shared Kernel must not have dependencies on any bounded context
rules.rationale: Shared Kernel must be context-independent — it is shared by all contexts and owned by none
rules.selects: Every crate with shared-kernel = true, whatever its layer.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate that carries a context.

rules.title: Modules must not access each other in the application layer
rules.rationale: An application layer talks to other modules through its own output ports, implemented by adapters - never directly. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not: an undeclared module must not be able to escape isolation by staying off the context map
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = application.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate of another context, that context's api and events crates included. Another context is a crate whose context is set and differs: a crate with a layer and no context (the shared kernel, bootstrap) is never another context, so every context may depend on the shared kernel; a shared-kernel crate is not selected - its dependency on a context is DCA-STR-002's.

rules.title: Modules must not access each other in the domain layer
rules.rationale: A domain layer talks to its own module and the shared kernel, nothing else - not even another module's api/. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = domain.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies name no crate of another context, that context's api and events crates included. Another context is a crate whose context is set and differs: a crate with a layer and no context (the shared kernel, bootstrap) is never another context, so every context may depend on the shared kernel; a shared-kernel crate is not selected - its dependency on a context is DCA-STR-002's.

rules.title: Open Host Services must be published: in the api package or as an incoming adapter
rules.rationale: An Open Host Service is the protocol a context publishes for other contexts - in-process as its api/ package, over the network as an incoming adapter (REST, gRPC, MCP). It belongs at the context boundary, never in the domain or application layer; the adapter's sub-package is irrelevant
rules.selects: Types that implement the OpenHostService marker and traits that carry it.
rules.checks: Each sits in an api crate or in the incoming module of an adapters crate.

rules.title: Outgoing adapters accessing other modules must only use their published api/ and events/ packages
rules.rationale: Cross-module communication goes through the target's published api/ (synchronous) and events/ (asynchronous) packages - DCA's in-process contract convention, package names rather than framework annotations - never through its domain, application, adapter or infrastructure packages. Selects structurally over every module that owns a DCA layer, declared as a bounded context or not
rules.selects: Every crate with layer = adapters.
rules.checks: Its Cargo dependencies on another context name that context's api and events crates only. A foreign domain, application or adapters crate is refused by the graph test; anything those crates do not export is refused by the compiler. Another context is a crate whose context is set and differs: a crate with a layer and no context (the shared kernel, bootstrap) is never another context, so every context may depend on the shared kernel; a shared-kernel crate is not selected - its dependency on a context is DCA-STR-002's.

rules.title: Integration event contracts reside in the configured events segment
rules.rationale: Integration contracts are published separately from translators and transport adapters
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: Each sits in a context's events crate (layer = events) - its published contract, a crate beside its api crate as Java's {context}/events beside {context}/api; a module named events inside the api crate is not the place. Never in the shared kernel, which declares no events layer: an integration event is one context's contract, not shared domain; translator and publisher sit in the adapters. Java's ..events.. of a module root also matches the shared kernel; the Rust reading follows the decision that the kernel holds none.

rules.title: Integration Events should have immutable shape
rules.rationale: An integration event is a published contract: once another context has read it, its shape may only grow, never change under an existing reader. A mutable event cannot make that promise - any holder can rewrite what a second consumer will read
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type. Its fields may be pub - a deliberate Rust reading: an integration event is the published record another context reads and builds, its fields are its contract, and a value held by another crate cannot be changed through a shared reference.

rules.title: Diagnostic: Event Listeners consuming integration events should use Anti-Corruption Layer
rules.rationale: Consumed integration events are translated into the consuming context's own language before they reach its domain — verified by code review, not statically
rules.selects: Informational - selects nothing.
rules.checks: Nothing is asserted. Whether a consumed integration event is translated before it reaches the domain is a review check.

rules.title: At least one bounded context is declared
rules.rationale: Without a declared context the context-map and isolation rules select nothing and report success over an empty model; a project without production code has no model to be empty, so it passes
rules.selects: The workspace members.
rules.checks: At least one crate carries a context in [package.metadata.dca]. A workspace that holds no production code yet passes: no crate has an item outside #[cfg(test)] in the module tree of its library or binary target, a program entry point aside - test-only crates, a library root that holds nothing but comments and test modules, and a binary crate (no library target) whose root declares no module and whose only item is fn main, are no production code. Once one such item exists, the rule fails until a context is declared, so a workspace whose crates miss the declaration still fails.

rules.title: At least one module owns a DCA layer
rules.rationale: Without a discovered module root every rule that selects over the layers matches nothing and reports success over an empty model; a project without production code has no model to be empty, so it passes
rules.selects: The workspace members.
rules.checks: At least one crate carries one of the layers in [package.metadata.dca]. A workspace that holds no production code yet passes: no crate has an item outside #[cfg(test)] in the module tree of its library or binary target, a program entry point aside - test-only crates, a library root that holds nothing but comments and test modules, and a binary crate (no library target) whose root declares no module and whose only item is fn main, are no production code. Once one such item exists, the rule fails until a layer is declared, so a workspace whose crates miss the declaration still fails.

rules.title: Interfaces in a module's events package must extend IntegrationEvent
rules.rationale: Everything in the events package is a published event contract. An interface there is one a producer's integration event implements and a consumer receives; delivery is at least once, so the consumer needs the event's identity and occurrence time through that interface, not only the payload
rules.selects: Traits in every events crate.
rules.checks: Each carries the IntegrationEvent role.

rules.title: Upstream, ExternalUpstream, and Partnership may only be declared on bounded context packages
rules.rationale: Context map declarations are reserved for bounded contexts — only a context can be downstream of, or partner with, another
rules.selects: Every crate's [package.metadata.dca], read for its upstreams, external-upstreams and partnerships arrays of tables. The declarations: [[package.metadata.dca.upstreams]] with context, via (a list of api and events), translation (acl or conformist) and status (implemented, the default, or planned); [[package.metadata.dca.external-upstreams]] with name, interaction (outbound or inbound), translation, contract-crates (a list of package names) and status; [[package.metadata.dca.partnerships]] with context.
rules.checks: Only the crate that declares a context carries them: the context's domain crate, or, for a context without a domain crate, its crate that names no layer. A declaration on an application, adapters, api or infrastructure crate, or on a crate without a context, is reported; whether a declaration is well-formed is left to the other rules.

rules.title: ExternalUpstream declarations must be well-formed and unique per name and interaction
rules.rationale: The identity of an @ExternalUpstream declaration is (name, interaction); internal contexts are declared with @Upstream instead
rules.selects: Every external-upstreams entry of every declaring crate, reading name, interaction, translation and status.
rules.checks: name is not blank and not the name of a context of the workspace; interaction is outbound or inbound, translation acl or conformist, status implemented or planned; and the pair (name, interaction) occurs at most once per context. The same external system declared by two contexts is not reported; contract-crates is not checked here.

rules.title: Upstream declarations must reference an existing bounded context and never the declaring context itself
rules.rationale: A dangling or self-referencing upstream edge describes a relationship that cannot exist
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry of every declaring crate, reading context, translation and status. Planned entries are included.
rules.checks: context names a context some crate declares and not the declaring one; translation is acl or conformist and status implemented or planned. Whether any code depends on the target is not established here.

rules.title: Upstream declarations must be unique per context and channel, and via must not be empty
rules.rationale: The identity of an @Upstream declaration is (context, via); different translations per channel require separate annotations
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry of every declaring crate, reading context and via. Planned entries are included.
rules.checks: via holds at least one channel, each one api or events, and the pair (context, channel) occurs at most once among the entries of one context; two entries towards one context on different channels pass.

rules.title: Upstream declarations and the module declaration's allowed dependencies must agree
rules.rationale: Neither the context map nor the module boundary may know more than the other — an edge that exists only on one side is stale
rules.selects: Every declaring crate with its upstreams entries towards existing other contexts, planned ones included, and every normal Cargo dependency of the context's crates on another context's api or events crate.
rules.checks: The declared upstream contexts equal the contexts whose api or events crate a crate of the context depends on: a declared upstream no crate depends on is reported on the declaring crate, a dependency on an undeclared one on the depending crate. Cargo.toml is the module declaration in Rust; there is no second one to compare, and a dependency names a crate, not a channel - the channels are DCA-MAP-007's and DCA-MAP-011's.

rules.title: Implemented Upstream declarations must be backed by an actual code dependency
rules.rationale: A declared IMPLEMENTED edge without any real dependency is stale (or premature — then it is PLANNED) and would otherwise pass forever alongside an equally stale module boundary entry
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry with status implemented towards an existing other context, reading via. Planned entries and entries towards an unknown context are skipped.
rules.checks: For each channel in via, some module of some crate of the declaring context names a path into that channel of the target - its events crate for events, its api crate for api. Which crate holds the use is not checked here. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Anti-Corruption Layer: upstream contract types must stay inside the matching adapter
rules.rationale: The ACL sits where the dependency crosses the boundary — outgoing adapters for synchronous API calls, incoming adapters for consumed events — and translates the upstream contract into the context's own model there
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry with translation = acl towards an existing other context, reading via and, for the translation site, the status.
rules.checks: No crate of the declaring context other than its adapters crate has a normal dependency on the target's api or events crate; within the adapters crate, a path into the api channel sits only in the outgoing module and a path into the events channel only in the incoming module, for the channels the entry names. For an implemented entry, each channel the target publishes as a crate also has its translation site: some module on the matching side (outgoing for api, incoming for events) of an adapters crate of the context names both a path into that channel and a path into a crate of its own context with layer domain or application - the module stands for Java's class -, or two modules of that side share it: one names the channel, the other its own domain or application, and one of the two names the other (a listener and its translator). Whether the adapter translates beyond naming both is not established. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Conformist: upstream contract types must never reach the domain layer
rules.rationale: Conformism does not suspend domain purity — the domain layer stays free of foreign contract types
rules.selects: Every upstreams entry with translation = conformist towards an existing other context; the status is not consulted.
rules.checks: The declaring context's domain crate has no normal dependency on the target's api or events crate; the graph test refuses the Cargo.toml line, and without it the compiler refuses every path into the crate. DCA-STR-004 refuses the same dependency for every context, declared or not.

rules.title: External system contract types must respect the declared translation and interaction
rules.rationale: An external system's contract types are confined to the adapter where the exchange crosses the boundary (ACL) or at least kept out of the domain (Conformist)
rules.selects: Every external-upstreams entry that names contract-crates (package names; a crate outside the workspace counts by its name), reading translation and interaction; the status is not consulted. An entry without contract crates only documents the relationship.
rules.checks: With acl, no crate of the context but the adapters crate has a normal dependency on a contract crate, and within it only the matching module - outgoing for outbound, incoming for inbound - names a path into one, by its package name or by the name a renamed dependency gives it (feed = { package = "vendor-feed" }). With conformist, the domain crate has no normal dependency on one. That the adapter translates is not established. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Cross-context dependencies on published interfaces require an Upstream declaration
rules.rationale: Every real dependency on a foreign api/ or events/ package is a context-map edge and must be declared as such
rules.selects: Every normal Cargo dependency of a context's crate on another context's api or events crate, and every path its modules name into such a crate, with the channel the path lies in (the events crate: events; the api crate: api).
rules.checks: The declaring crate of the source context carries an upstreams entry for the target context - for a path, one whose via names that channel. Planned entries count as declared. Dependencies on a foreign context's other crates are not reported by this rule. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Partnership declarations must reference an existing bounded context, never themselves, and must be symmetric
rules.rationale: A partnership is a mutual commitment — it exists only when both contexts declare it
rules.selects: Every partnerships entry of every declaring crate, reading context.
rules.checks: It names a context some crate declares, not the declaring one, and the target's declaring crate carries a partnerships entry naming the declaring context in turn. A partnership grants no dependency.

rules.title: Diagnostic: Display declared context map
rules.rationale: Printing the declared edges makes the executable context map reviewable at a glance
rules.selects: Every upstreams, external-upstreams and partnerships entry of every declaring crate.
rules.checks: Informational - lists every declared edge with its channels or interaction and its translation, and the protocol, exchanges and rationale where declared, and never fails. The status is not printed.

rules.title: Every allowed dependency of a module declaration must be backed by an actual code dependency
rules.rationale: A context declares only the dependencies it uses. An allowed dependency no class uses is a door left open: the next dependency through it passes the module boundary without anyone deciding it
rules.selects: Every normal Cargo dependency of a context's crate on a crate of another context. A dependency on the api or events crate of a context the declaring crate names in a planned upstreams entry is skipped.
rules.checks: Some module of the crate names a path into the dependency. The rustc lint unused_crate_dependencies holds the same per crate for every dependency. Paths are read from use declarations - those inside function bodies and blocks too, whose scope is approximated by the whole module - and from every other item, the arguments of vec!, matches!, assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq!, debug_assert_ne!, format!, write!, writeln!, print!, println!, eprint!, eprintln! and panic! parsed as expressions (and the pattern of matches!). Not seen: paths inside any other macro invocation, and arguments of those macros that do not parse as expressions.

rules.title: Domain Events must implement DomainEvent and have immutable shape
rules.rationale: Domain events should have immutable state implementing DomainEvent (named in past tense, e.g., ProductCreated, CartCleared)
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: No method takes &mut self and no field type is an interior-mutability type. Implementing the trait is the selection itself.

rules.title: Domain Events must reside in domain package
rules.rationale: Domain events are part of the domain layer (named in past tense)
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: Each sits in a domain crate, the shared kernel's included.

rules.title: Domain events must not carry prohibited framework metadata
rules.rationale: Domain objects carry no metadata for container management, persistence or transaction coordination
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent in a domain crate, the shared kernel's included.
rules.checks: No derive and no attribute from the configured framework crates (persistence, web, injection) on the type, its fields, its variants, its impl blocks or their methods. A domain crate that does not depend on such a crate cannot name the derive at all (DCA-ONI-002); the source test holds the case where the project allows the crate in the domain.

rules.title: Integration Events must be annotated with IntegrationEventType
rules.rationale: @IntegrationEventType(name, version) is the contract identity of every integration event — the serializer keys (name, version) to the class and stamps both onto the wire envelope
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: The trait requires the associated constants TYPE and VERSION, so the compiler refuses an integration event without its type metadata. Rust has no annotations; the constants are the metadata.

rules.title: Integration events carry the schema version in their type metadata, not in the payload
rules.rationale: The schema version is a class property (@IntegrationEventType), never per-instance payload data — an explicit schema-version data field duplicates the annotation and can drift from it
rules.selects: Types that implement IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: No field is named schema_version, event_version or contract_version.

rules.title: Domain events that are not integration events carry no schema version
rules.rationale: Versioning is a contract concern of integration events — a purely internal domain event has no wire contract to version
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent but not IntegrationEvent.
rules.checks: No field is named schema_version, event_version or contract_version.

rules.title: Domain Events must have a timestamp field
rules.rationale: An event records something that happened — without a timestamp the fact cannot be ordered, replayed or audited
rules.selects: Types that implement DomainEvent.
rules.checks: The trait requires occurred_on(); the source test checks that a field whose type names one of the configured timestamp types ([workspace.metadata.dca] timestamp-types; Timestamp, SystemTime, DateTime and OffsetDateTime by default), generic arguments included (Option<Timestamp>), backs it - on an enum, in every variant or through a variant that carries an event type of its own.

rules.title: Aggregates, entities and value objects must not use domain services
rules.rationale: A domain service exists for logic that spans several aggregates, so the application calls it; a model type that reaches for one would drive another aggregate from inside its own
rules.selects: Methods of types that implement AggregateRoot, Entity or Value.
rules.checks: No method body calls a function of, or constructs, a type that implements DomainService, nor calls a method on one held in a parameter (through its generic bounds), a field of self, or a local binding whose type is written out or that is initialised with one. A parameter of that type alone is not reported.

rules.title: Domain service operations take an aggregate or an entity
rules.rationale: A domain service works on the model itself; an operation that only takes extracted values moves the decision out of the domain and into its caller
rules.selects: pub methods with a receiver of types that implement DomainService. A type's methods are, as Java reads a class's: its inherent methods and the methods of its impls of workspace traits; impls of std, core, external and building-block traits are not read.
rules.checks: At least one parameter is, by value or by reference, a type that implements AggregateRoot or Entity.

rules.title: Domain services are used only by the application and by other domain services
rules.rationale: A domain service holds logic that spans aggregates, and the use case decides when it runs and puts its outcome into the result. A model type, a read model, an adapter or the composition root that calls one takes that decision outside the application - the incoming adapter and the model type are each held by a narrower rule too (DCA-HEX-012, DCA-ADV-019)
rules.selects: Every function body - free functions and the methods of impl blocks - in every crate except the application crates, the impls of a type that implements DomainService excluded. A domain service is a type that implements DomainService, as DCA-ADV-010 selects it: Rust marks no module, so a module of free functions is no domain service by this rule.
rules.checks: No body names a type that implements DomainService as an expression (a struct literal, a unit value, an associated function), nor calls a method on a parameter, a local binding or a field of self whose type implements it, nor on one built in place. In an infrastructure or bootstrap crate - the composition root - a construction (a struct literal, a unit value, an associated function without a receiver that returns Self or the type by its name) passes; a call there is reported. A parameter or a field of that type alone is not reported; a call through a generic bound or a trait object is not seen.

rules.title: The base InputPort contract is not redeclared in the project
rules.rationale: Base InputPort interface defines the generic contract for all use cases (Hexagonal Architecture)
rules.selects: Traits named InputPort anywhere in the workspace.
rules.checks: None outside the building blocks.
